Least-squares AMMI model

Source: R/ge_ammi.R
bys_ls_ammi.Rd

bys_ls_ammi() computes the least-squares estimates of the AMMI model with all interaction axes: grand mean, genotype and environment effects, singular values and vectors of the interaction, and the error variance. They are the starting values of bayes_ammi() and the classical estimates it is compared with.

Usage

bys_ls_ammi(.data, .y, .gen, .env, .rep)

# Default S3 method
bys_ls_ammi(.data, .y, .gen, .env, .rep)

Arguments

.data

a data frame with one row per plot.

.y, .gen, .env, .rep

the columns of the response, genotypes, environments and replicates: bare names, strings or vectors.

Value

A list (class c("bys_ge_ammi", "bys_result", "list")) with the components of the earlier versions:

g, e, Rep, k

numbers of genotypes, environments, replicates and axes.

ge_means

the result of bys_ls_means().

mu, sigma2, tau

grand mean, error variance and its reciprocal (precision).

tao, delta

genotype and environment effects (bys_ls_gen_effects(), bys_ls_env_effects()).

lambdas, alphas, gammas

singular values and genotype and environment singular vectors of the interaction.

Details

With the cell means \(\bar{y}_{ij}\) of \(B\) replicates, \(\hat{\mu} = \bar{y}\), \(\hat{\tau}_i = \bar{y}_{i\cdot} - \bar{y}\), \(\hat{\delta}_j = \bar{y}_{\cdot j} - \bar{y}\) and the singular value decomposition of the interaction effects (bys_ls_ge_effects()), \(K = \min(G, E) - 1\) axes. The error variance is the residual variance of the model with random replicates within environments (bys_ls_model()), in closed form for balanced data: $$\hat{\sigma}^2 = \frac{\mathrm{SSW} - \mathrm{SS}_{B(E)}}{E(B - 1)(G - 1)}$$ when the replicate mean square is not smaller, otherwise (the replicate variance component estimated as zero) \(\mathrm{SSW}/(GE(B - 1))\); SSW is the within-cell and \(\mathrm{SS}_{B(E)}\) the replicate-within-environment sum of squares.

Change from the earlier versions. The error variance came from lme4::lmer(); the closed form gives the same value for balanced data without needing lme4.

References

Crossa, J., Perez-Elizalde, S., Jarquin, D., Cotes, J. M., Viele, K., Liu, G. and Cornelius, P. L. (2011). Bayesian estimation of the additive main effects and multiplicative interaction model. \emphCrop Science, \strong51(4), 1458–1469. \doi10.2135/cropsci2010.06.0343

Gauch, H. G. (1992). Statistical Analysis of Regional Yield Trials: AMMI Analysis of Factorial Designs. Elsevier, Amsterdam.

See also

bayes_ammi, bys_ls_ge_effects

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

data(cultivo2009)
fit <-
  bys_ls_ammi(
      .data = cultivo2009
    , .y    = y
    , .gen  = entry
    , .env  = site
    , .rep  = rep
    )
fit$lambdas
#>  [1] 5204.1759 3885.7373 3740.4723 2777.3430 2704.3153 2106.1909 1881.7436
#>  [8] 1874.5398 1362.9746  973.6497  827.5602
fit$sigma2
#> [1] 589051.8
